text:
kai: Strange one from the python onboarding run today. Async handler does an auth retry by scheduling a background task and sometimes that background task emits a log with a different req_id and the PII redaction never ran for that emit. Repro + notes below.

neha: can you paste the minimal logs and the SDK init from the sampleapp?

kai: sanitized excerpt from asyncio sampleapp:
```
INFO 2026-12-02T16:20:01Z req=hn-11 user=lee@example.com step=auth.start
INFO 2026-12-02T16:20:02Z req=hn-11 step=auth.retry attempt=1
INFO 2026-12-02T16:20:03Z req=bg-77 user=lee@example.com step=auth.background.cleanup
```
first two look redacted/ok, last one leaked the email and has a bg-specific req id. SDK init in the sample application:
```py
Telemetry.configure(hooks=[otel_hook, redact_hook, autosample])
```
I think problem is twofold: (1) retry spawns an asyncio.create_task which loses the original contextvar/span, and (2) our redact_hook is attached to span start rather than the record emitter, so background tasks that create fresh records bypass it.

paul: interesting, this isn't the express re-dispatch pattern we've been seeing. this is an async-context-loss + attach-vs-emit issue. python contextvars + asyncio tasks will drop the current context unless you explicitly copy Context. Did the sampleapp use context.copy() when creating the task?

kai: no, minimal sampleapp didn't, it just create_task()s a cleanup handler after retry. patching sampleapp to pass context preserved the req id but still relied on attach-time redaction. When I modified the SDK in the app to run redaction on emit the leak went away even if the background task created a fresh req id. quick local change: 
```py
# patch in sample app logger
def on_emit(record):
    if not getattr(record, '_pii_redacted', False):
        redact_pii(record)
        setattr(record, '_pii_redacted', True)
logger.add_emit_hook(on_emit)
```
fixed leak in local runs.

neha: thanks. two different mitigation paths: (A) educate customers to preserve context when scheduling background tasks (i.e., copy contextvars or use helper wrapper), (B) change SDK default to run redact at emit-time for python too, or (C) make redact idempotent and inexpensive and run both at attach + emit.

paul: another thought: we should also detect common background-task frameworks (celery, rq, asyncio.create_task) and provide small wrappers in the SDK that preserve req headers and context automatically. that reduces friction for onboarding.

kai: agree. for python specifically we should also mention ContextVar handling in onboarding docs. sampleapp patch attached to repro.

ota-bot: created ticket DE-9002: "python async: background task loses context -> req_id drift and missed redaction" - https://jira/redwood/DE-9002 :warning:

neha: proposed plan: 1) add an integration test that simulates asyncio.create_task path + retry + background emit and assert single stable req id or no raw emails in logs; 2) add emit-stage redaction in python SDK with a cheap _pii_redacted marker to avoid double work; 3) add a helper wrapper function for create_task that preserves ContextVars (and a shim for common job queues); 4) update onboarding docs to call out contextvar preservation and the new helper; 5) ship 1.3.1-canary for python SDK and monitor PII alerts.

paul: i'll own the create_task wrapper and a small shim for aiohttp sampleapp. neha, can you own the SDK emit-hook change + microbench?

neha: will do. I'll include a benchmark showing emit-time redaction overhead under a heavy background-task churn load. if it's significant we can add a heuristic to only run emit redaction when a record has fields matching looks_like_pii.

kai: good call. one more edge: tracing exporters that buffer and re-emit spans asynchronously could also trigger this, so include a test that buffers and flushes later.

oncall: acked for visibility, will watch DE-9002 and chime if alerts spike after canary.

neha: thanks all. i'll open the PR and link the integration test. kai, please paste the small sampleapp repro into the ticket.
